title: Jason Calacanis on disrupting conferences, product focus, and when to take the exit
summary: A 2011 Startup Grind fireside where Jason explains how he undercut pay-to-pitch conferences, why resilience and product focus matter most, and when to ignore advice. He also argues founders should take big exit offers and ignore the press, drawing on his own $20M mistake.

principles.text: Resilience and resourcefulness are the top entrepreneur traits, and he hires on them.
principles.quote: Perseverance, resilience, and resourcefulness are the most important traits of an entrepreneur.

principles.text: Change the rules when you can't win the game as it stands; fight the fight you can win.
principles.quote: fight the fight you can win and if you can't win, just change the rules of the game.

principles.text: Pick ideas most people don't yet get. If everyone likes it, it's already tried or too small.
principles.quote: if the majority of people understand the idea and think it’s a good idea I have absolutely no interest in doing it because it means by default that everyone has that idea

principles.text: Success comes from focusing on the product; test it by asking whether people get repeated value.
principles.quote: At the end of the day it’s all about product. All of my success in life has come when I've focused on the product and made something that people connected with

principles.text: To beat an incumbent in search or similar categories, you must be 2-3x better, not 10-20% better.
principles.quote: you have to make something 2-3 times better, I'm convinced, in order for people to switch. The mental cost of switch is high, people think it’s low.

principles.text: Take a disproportionate exit offer; passing on big money often means ending with nothing.
principles.quote: If they offer you $100 million, take the money for God's sake!
